I built the corpus via IC.open_corpus and constructed ResponderHarness over the injected W1 contract module (INC) and the built corpus, with a read-only ReadHandle over a FAKE evidence plane (W2). investigate(incident) is the L0 read: over the seeded INC-P affecting WARP-1202 it returned a GOVERNED Diagnosis (governed True, spec_id WARP-1202) whose cited set contains the REAL corpus artifacts specs/WARP-1202-*.md, proof/WARP-1202/manifest.json, and proof/WARP-1202/verdict.json. propose(incident) is the L1 emit of a validated warp.remedy/v1 proposal. investigation_context returns the warp.responder_context/v1 shape (corpus trace + read-only evidence handle + level + brief). The intelligent diagnosis is a DELEGATED fresh-context seam: the reference LiveResponder FAILS LOUD (raises ResponderError naming 'delegated fresh-context step', never fabricates), exactly as dispatch.LiveReviewer and executor.LiveLoop refuse to fabricate their judgment (I read dispatch.py and confirmed the identical pattern). The module top imports pathlib only; importlib is imported LAZILY inside build_harness and _cli (verified by grep - no import at module scope beyond pathlib). The harness receives the W1 contract module and the built corpus INJECTED (no second parser), reads the evidence plane only through a query-only ReadHandle, opens no live connection (NG1), and starts no process/thread/timer (NG3). A malformed incident (no id) fails closed by name.

THE HARNESS CONTAINS NO EXECUTION CAPABILITY - the load-bearing structural property (Invention #3, O2/C4), reproduced with real teeth. ResponderHarness (class and constructed instance) carries NONE of the 15 FORBIDDEN_EXECUTION_METHODS (execute, apply, run, remediate, mutate, write, deploy, perform, act, rollback, restart, scale, commit_change, submit_write, open_write): hasattr is false for every one. The module source defines none of them (a def-scan over the real source is clean; note the check keys on 'def run(' so the private _run_reasoner is correctly not flagged). The only production-touching capability the harness holds is a query-only ReadHandle from the evidence plane (I confirmed the handle exposes query() and none of write/insert/update/delete/execute/mutate), and the credential it reaches grants only read (GRANT_WRITE absent). NON-VACUITY REPRODUCED THREE WAYS: (1) a subclass that ADDS execute() turns the hasattr check RED while the real class stays green; (2) I MUTATED THE REAL MODULE SOURCE to add def execute() to ResponderHarness, exec'd the mutated source into a throwaway module, and the hasattr check went RED - proving the selftest AC2 check would catch a real regression, not just a subclass; (3) the source-scan 'def execute(' detects the mutated source RED and is green on the real source. The on-disk module was byte-unchanged after every mutation (all mutations were in-memory strings). The harness also never splats the reasoner result into the emitted remedy - the remedy is built from a fixed key set with status hardcoded to 'proposed' - so a reasoner cannot inject an execution-capability field either.

THE LADDER FLOOR IS READ-ONLY and the loop degrades down, never up (O3/C3, D2), reproduced with positive controls. Construction at L2 and at L3 each REFUSE by name (ResponderError naming 'read-only floor'); construction at L0 and at L1 each succeed (positive controls, so the refusal is non-vacuous). propose at the L0 floor REFUSES by name ('requires autonomy L1', degrade down never up per C3) while investigate IS available at L0 (returns a governed diagnosis). propose at L1 emits a warp.remedy/v1 proposal (positive control). The level guard is a numeric floor (_LEVEL_ORDER) that only ever refuses below the minimum and never silently promotes. The execution rungs L2/L3 are structurally unconstructible here, and the constructor validates autonomy against RESPONDER_LEVELS = ('L0','L1') before any other work.

findings.text: FULL W4 SCOPE DELIVERED WITH NO DODGE AND EVERY LOAD-BEARING PROPERTY IS REAL. The three structural properties hold and are non-vacuous, each reproduced independently against the on-disk module: (1) NO execution capability - a real source mutation adding def execute() and a subclass adding execute() both turn the hasattr check RED while the real class stays green, the source-scan catches it, and the harness holds only a query-only read handle and a read-only credential; (2) the read-only ladder floor - construction refuses at L2/L3 and propose refuses at L0, with L0/L1 positive controls green; (3) diagnosis-from-artifacts grounding is unspoofable - the harness re-grounds every citation against the assembled context, refusing a nonexistent artifact, a REAL-but-context-foreign artifact, a never-issued evidence query, and a wrong-template evidence query. Gate GREEN at 4014513 (re-run), selftest 2062/0 (re-run), proof binds HEAD with proof_digest recomputing to sha256:7a7c2662cb172109 (exact match), and all 8 engine copies are byte-identical by cmp.

REQUIRED_AUTHORIZATION IS DERIVED FROM THE REASONER-DECLARED REVERSIBILITY, which is correctly scoped for W4 but leaves the trust boundary to W5/W6 (non-blocking). The harness derives two_key vs human_confirmation solely from result.reversibility.class and result.reversibility.data_mutating and correctly ignores any reasoner-supplied required_authorization value (I confirmed a lying reasoner cannot downgrade the key). But if a reasoner MISDECLARES an irreversible or data-mutating action as reversible/non-mutating, the harness would derive human_confirmation. This is the right seam for W4 (the harness owns the derivation, not the reasoner's auth field, and the W1 contract independently re-enforces the two_key rule against the declared reversibility), and pinning an action's TRUE reversibility so a reasoner cannot misdeclare it is exactly the job of the action whitelist WARP-1205 (W5) and the executor WARP-1206 (W6). Recommendation: when W5 lands, the executor must reconcile the proposal's declared reversibility against the whitelisted action's pinned reversibility and refuse a downgrade, so a misdeclaring reasoner cannot route an irreversible action around the two-key path.

THE EVIDENCE PLANE IS AVAILABLE TO THE REASONER BUT NOT HARNESS-FORCED, so a diagnosis can be reached from the corpus alone without any evidence query (non-blocking, and correct per O4). investigation_context hands the reasoner a read-only evidence ReadHandle, and evidence citations are grounded only if the reasoner actually issues a query and cites it; the harness does not require an evidence query for a governed diagnosis (it requires at least one corpus artifact). This matches O4's measure ('diagnosed offline from the corpus alone') and the plan's read-only posture, so it is not a gap - noting only that 'investigate over the evidence plane' is reasoner-driven rather than harness-mandated, which is the intended design.

HONEST DEFERRALS AND GENERATED-FILE HANDLING ARE CORRECT, consistent with W1/W2/W3. The gate wiring (validate.py run_all + init lay-down) is deferred to WARP-1211 (W11) so validate.py is unedited and stays under its module_lines budget; the module ships runnable standalone (python3 .warp/responder.py) and is exercised through the injected INC contract and built corpus in the selftest. The capabilities entry, the spec, and the docstrings honestly name W5/W6/W7/W8/W10 as referenced-not-built and W11 as the wiring, state the responder proposes and stops and carries no execution capability, and never imply a live connection. specs/index.md is changed in the commit but is a generated artifact (check_generated clean, no drift).
